title: Rights — 8 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Rights. 8 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/rights.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). One further declaration closes by rfl, checked by evaluation, and is not included here, by design. Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 58 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: instruments (8), claim (7), idOf (4), kindOf (3).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/rights.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 8 sealed receipts fold to 6ae9baad-d17f-8059-be52-438399bff840. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 0, 2, 5, 1, 5, 5). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: energy.lean (4 observed, 1.95 expected, lift 2.06), nim.lean (4 observed, 1.95 expected, lift 2.06), imagined.lean (15 observed, 8.2 expected, lift 1.83). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.08 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 90.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.93; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.43. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 7b6ebaaa9854 (2026-09-15), over 807 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. This file already NAMED its prior art in prose while the attribution table recorded none. The legal instruments are external and long-standing: the Berne Convention Art. 5(2) ("the enjoyment and the exercise of these rights shall not be subject to any formality"), the moral rights of Art. 6bis, and the sui generis database right of Directive 96/9/EC. claims_exactly_what_arises_without_formality and the_claimed_are_copyright_moral_rights_and_the_database rest entirely on them. Bounded: what is not prior art is the enumeration of instruments FOR THIS DEPOSIT and the decision, by exhaustion, that the set it claims is exactly the without-formality set. The law is not this deposit's; the audit of its own position against the law is. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. claims_exactly_what_arises_without_formality — instruments.all (fun r => auto r == claim r) record
  2. the_claimed_are_copyright_moral_rights_and_the_database — ([1, 2, 3] : List Nat).all (fun i => ((instruments.filter claim).map idOf).contains i) record
  3. the_claimed_set_is_exactly_those_three_and_the_unregistered_mark — ([1, 2, 3, 8] : List Nat).all (fun i => ((instruments.filter claim).map idOf).contains i) record
  4. the_unclaimed_are_the_registry_the_excluded_and_the_unownable — (instruments.filter (fun r => ¬ claim r)).map idOf = [4, 5, 6, 7] record
  5. no_right_that_needs_a_registry_act_is_claimed — (instruments.filter (fun r => kindOf r == 1)).all (fun r => claim r == false) record
  6. no_excluded_subject_matter_is_claimed — (instruments.filter (fun r => kindOf r == 2)).all (fun r => claim r == false) record
  7. nothing_incapable_of_ownership_is_claimed — (instruments.filter (fun r => kindOf r == 3)).all (fun r => claim r == false) record
  8. the_enumeration_is_complete_and_unduplicated — instruments.map idOf = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 7b6ebaaa9854 and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
